- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.30) over 3+ days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to counter mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean-reverting dips; if price drops below 70.0 and sentiment is neutral, forecast should not fall below 70.5 unless strong negative sentiment persists.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment turns sharply positive.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term volatility (e.g., alternating +0.00/-0.00), model tends to smooth too much; allow 1–2% volatility in forecast to reflect sentiment noise.
